The probe offset is one pixel below the upper link's own text and no more: the lower link's padded box starts two pixels below that text, so +1 is inside the upper link's padding and +2 is already the lower link's. The offset is computed from the text rect every run, never from the anchor's padded box, which would move with the padding it measures.

A trial click's position is measured from the padding box, so the same returned offset is outside the anchor once the padding is gone - that is what makes the check mutation-sensitive, and the failure arrives as a bounded 5 s actionability timeout naming the element that intercepted the point, not as a string comparison.

The settle is not redundant with Playwright's own scrolled-into-view check: Playwright scrolls only an element outside the viewport, and the flake's turn is inside the viewport and behind a fixed composer. Remove the settle and the trial click waits out its timeout in exactly the 1-in-3 runs that used to fail.
